dependencies.statement:
Let $P$ be an admissible polygon whose boundary segments are all effective edges, and assume the edge moments in @lem-edge-moments. Then its first eigenfunction satisfies
$$
\int_P|\nabla u|^4=\lambda^2\left(\int_Pu^4-A(P)^{-1}\right).
$$
dependencies.title: Airy fourth-power identity

target.proof:
The domain-independent Dirichlet heat-kernel estimate gives $\|u\|_\infty^2\le e^2\lambda/(8\pi)$ for the normalized first eigenfunction. Under the edge-moment hypotheses, @lem-airy-identity applies, and $\int_Pu^4\le\|u\|_\infty^2\int_Pu^2=\|u\|_\infty^2$; combining these facts yields
$$
\int_P|\nabla u|^4\le \frac{e^2\lambda^3}{8\pi}.
$$
The same $L^\infty$ bound gives $\int_P|u|^4\le\|u\|_\infty^2$, so the $W^{1,4}(P)$ norm is bounded by a constant depending only on $A_0$ and $\Lambda$. Since $u\in H^1_0(P)$, its zero extension has no boundary distribution term in its weak gradient; the extension therefore lies in $W^{1,4}(\mathbb R^2)$ with the same gradient bound. Morrey's inequality in dimension two then gives a $C^{0,1/2}$ representative with the same parameter dependence.
target.statement: For every fixed area $A_0>0$ and eigenvalue bound $\Lambda<\infty$, there is $C=C(A_0,\Lambda)$ such that every admissible stationary polygon satisfying the edge-moment hypotheses of @lem-edge-moments, with $A(P)=A_0$ and $\lambda_1(P)\le\Lambda$, has its zero extension $\bar u$ of the $L^2(P)$-normalized positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction uniformly bounded in $W^{1,4}(\mathbb R^2)$ and hence in $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb R^2)$.
target.title: Uniform W1,4 bound

critical_errors: @lem-airy-identity requires that the boundary segments are all effective edges. The proof only invokes the identity from the edge-moment hypotheses and never shows that every target polygon satisfies this additional condition; hence the key fourth-power gradient estimate is unsupported for the stated class.
gaps: The exact domain-independent heat-kernel estimate is asserted without identifying the heat-kernel bound and semigroup argument that yield its constant.
The zero-extension claim implicitly uses the trace/zero-extension theorem for W^{1,4} functions on polygonal (Lipschitz) domains; this is standard but should be stated.
nonblocking_comments: The resulting bounds may be independent of A_0, which is still compatible with a constant written as C(A_0,Λ).
report.repair_hints: Either add the all-effective-edges hypothesis to the target or explicitly establish that it follows from admissibility. Then spell out the heat-kernel semigroup estimate and the W^{1,4} zero-extension fact for polygonal domains.
report.summary: The argument has the right analytic estimates, but it applies @lem-airy-identity without establishing all of that lemma’s hypotheses. In particular, the dependency requires every boundary segment to be an effective edge, which is not stated in the target assumptions or justified in the proof.
